parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Rearrange the formula to make $p$ the subject.

solution:
(a) Square both sides: $q^2 = \frac{p + 2r}{p - r}$.
Multiply by $(p - r)$: $q^2(p - r) = p + 2r$
$q^2 p - q^2 r = p + 2r$
Collect the terms in $p$ on one side: $q^2 p - p = 2r + q^2 r$
$p(q^2 - 1) = r(q^2 + 2)$
$p = \frac{r(q^2 + 2)}{q^2 - 1}$.

(b) $p = \frac{8(3^2 + 2)}{3^2 - 1} = \frac{8 \times 11}{8} = 11$.
Check: $\sqrt{\frac{11 + 16}{11 - 8}} = \sqrt{9} = 3$.
syllabus_check: 4052 Algebraic expressions and formulae: changing the subject of a formula in which the new subject appears twice inside a square root — square, clear the fraction, collect like terms, factorise, divide (a); substitution into the rearranged formula (b). No topic outside 4052. Marks 3 + 1 = 4 match the slot.
originality_note: The exemplars rearrange fractional formulae with the subject on both sides (2025 P1 Q18, 2022 P1 Q20), an x^2 fraction (2018 P1 Q17), or evaluate first and rearrange second (2024 P1 Q12, 2023 P2 Q2(c)). This formula has the subject twice under a square root, so the first step is squaring rather than cross-multiplying, and the part order is reversed: the rearrangement comes first and the numerical part uses it. New letters, new structure, new numbers; no other question in the paper changes the subject of a formula.
